answer: Witnessed Session Quorum. Each identity holds a hardware vault whose private key signs every action, so keys cannot be mass-copied. An anchor record binds that key to a witnessed session: two independent operators must co-sign a live challenge, one holding a quill that writes entropy into the record. Enforced by accepting only actions whose session transcript carries both signatures within a fixed clock window. A sybil therefore needs two real, separately present humans and a physical device per identity, paid in coordination time and hardware, not just software clones.
